notes: Van Tilburg (arXiv:2006.12431) introduces the 'stellar basin' concept: gravitationally bound axions emitted by the Sun accumulate over ~10^7 yr, giving a local density independent of DM assumptions. The paper recasts XENON1T S2-only (and S1+S2, LUX, PandaX-II) axion-DM absorption line searches via Eq. 28 into a NEW conservative exclusion on g_aee (blue region of Fig. 3), using the conservative ejection timescale tau~1e7 yr. No numerical table is provided; data_points are approximate values read off the described Fig. 3 conservative boundary (e.g., the text states the conservative limit crosses g_aee~2.6-3.7e-12 near m~0.7 keV, and the exclusion spans roughly 0.5-30 keV). No local DM density assumption applies since the basin density (not rho_DM) sources the signal; rho_DM=0.3-0.45 GeV/cm^3 only enters via the recasting ratio of the original DM search. Extraction confidence limited by figure-only data; values uncertain to factor ~2.
